# April 29, 2026

Training on the merged TCGA_PAAD (RNA-seq) + CPTAC (proteomics) cohort ($n=273$), the model kept
returning $\hat\beta_k = 0$ for every factor. It reconstructed expression fine but learned no
survival signal at all, so risk prediction was just a constant hazard. This entry covers the
diagnosis and the first fix.

## Method updates

- **Preprocessing fix.** The original pipeline selected the top 2,000 variable genes within each
  cohort *before* intersecting gene universes across platforms, which left only ~838 genes shared
  between the two. Intersecting the raw gene universes first, before any variance filtering, grew
  the shared feature set to the full 2,000.
- **Four in-model changes ("Cluster A")**, adopted together after ruling out simpler fixes ($\lambda$
  sweeps, high $\lambda$, EBMF warm-starts all failed to rescue $\beta$): reordering the inner CAVI
  loop so $\beta$ updates before $L$ and $F$; a short $\beta$-only burn-in; an $\alpha$ warmup
  schedule; and `normalize_AB`, which rescales the survival precision term in the $L$-update. That
  last one mattered most: at iteration 1 on the merged cohort, the survival term carried roughly
  $0$–$2\times10^{-4}$ of the weight of the genomics term, so survival had essentially no say in the
  loading update without it.

## Results updates

The Cluster A changes fixed the training-side collapse: the merged fit now converges to a stable
solution with 2 of 20 factors active, non-degenerate loadings, and a monotone ELBO. An unsupervised
EBMF diagnostic on the same matrix confirmed there's real signal to find. 5 of 20 factors came back
survival-associated, with the strongest hitting C-index 0.629 at $p=3\times10^{-6}$, so real
survival signal was present in the data.

The catch: external validation got *worse* on 4 of 5 cohorts after Cluster A, relative to the
pre-Cluster-A merged fit (Dijk 0.606 vs. 0.626, PACA-AU array 0.576 vs. 0.636, PACA-AU seq 0.629 vs.
0.653, Puleo 0.550 vs. 0.626; only Moffitt improved, 0.541 vs. 0.529). For context, single-cohort
training (no merging at all) was already reaching external C-index in the 0.60–0.63 range, so that's
the bar merged training needs to clear.

## Relevance of new findings

Cluster A solved the optimization failure but not the actual goal. The model can now produce
non-zero survival coefficients on the merged training set, but those coefficients fit the training
Cox objective without transporting to new cohorts. A fit with low training error that doesn't
generalize is not progress on the problem we actually care about. That points at something more
structural than a tuning issue.

## Open items to address

- Why does a training fit that's no longer collapsed still generalize worse than single-cohort
  training? The current best guess is that the fix recovered factors aligned to *this* training set's
  Cox objective rather than to biology that holds up across platforms.
- Next step: move development to a `cox-on-YF-reformulation` branch and implement Cox-on-$YF$
  ($\eta=(YF)\beta$ in place of $\eta=L\beta$), so training and prediction use the same observed-data
  projection instead of the LB approximation. This needs fresh derivations, not just a tuning pass.
